title: Chapter 12: Files, NIO, Date-Time, Regex, and Serialization
description: Cross file, text, time, and serialization boundaries explicitly. Learners constrain resolved paths to an approved root, stream bytes and characters with declared UTF-8 encoding, select correct java.time types and inject Clock, design and test bounded regular expressions, and version serialization schemas without exposing implementation objects or enabling native-deserialization attacks.

exercises.title: Path, Files, traversal defense, metadata, and atomic moves: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Does normalize plus startsWith alone handle symlink escapes?
choices: Yes; Path objects cannot name links
No; filesystem link and race policies remain necessary
Yes; normalization resolves every symlink securely
hints: normalize() and startsWith() only reason about the lexical path text; they cannot detect that a component resolves through a symbolic link to a location outside the root.

exercises.instructionMarkdown: What differs between matches and find?
hints: matches() requires the pattern to consume the entire input region, while find() searches for the next matching subsequence and can succeed on only part of the input.

exercises.title: Chapter 12 implementation lab: courseCode
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Implement `courseCode`. Accept exactly two uppercase ASCII letters, a hyphen, and four digits. Write the precondition and boundary table first, keep the method deterministic, and do not print.

Use whole-input matching and ASCII letters/digits, not a substring search.
hints: Require the pattern to match the whole string, not merely be contained in it: two uppercase ASCII letters, a hyphen, then exactly four digits.
Test a lowercase code, an extra prefix or suffix, the wrong digit count, and the exact minimum-length boundary before submitting.

exercises.title: Whole-region grammar
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Repair the regex check so it validates the entire input region instead of finding a matching substring inside `prefix JV-0021`, and the program writes exactly `false`. Keep the same compiled pattern and explain why matches() versus find() changes the outcome, rather than hard-coding the print statement. Output tests verify the printed result; confirming whole-input validation actually happens requires reading the source.
hints: The requirement validates the entire input, not a matching substring.
